text:
Maya: quick sync — need to lock ordering for Optimize toolkit: quantization, batching, caching. Customer A and some enterprise prospects are pushing for quant first. thoughts? :thinking_face:
Jordan: Agree quant gives biggest unit cost win for long-tail gen workloads. But eng effort depends on backend kernel work + quant-aware perf tests.
Priya: From model side: 8-bit/q4x gives 2-2.5x throughput for many models, but quality regressions vary by model/family. We should require a small eval harness per model class.
Carlos: infra note — caching (KV/prefix) has infra surface area (state routing, eviction, multi-tenant safety). Lower dev lift than kernel-level quant but ops burden higher.
Lee: Customers keep asking for predictable latency + cost. Batching helps latency tail at scale (throughput-latency tradeoff). For PLG usage, caching early prefixes can reduce burst costs quickly.
Maya: I'm thinking we apply RICE to get objective ordering. Draft numbers (quick and dirty):
```
Quantization: Reach=60, Impact=8, Confidence=0.6, Effort=3 -> RICE~960
Batching: Reach=80, Impact=6, Confidence=0.7, Effort=4 -> RICE~840
Caching: Reach=70, Impact=5, Confidence=0.5, Effort=2 -> RICE~350
```
Maya: Notes — Reach = percent of calls affected; Impact = relative unit-cost or latency improvement; Confidence = how sure we are; Effort = dev+infra weeks.
Jordan: Those numbers look fine as a starting point. I'd push quant out as spike -> prototype -> canary flow. Spike = 2w kernel/ci work + small perf harness.
Priya: Agree. Spike should include eval on our benchmark set (conversational, instruction, embeddings) and automated quality regression gate (e.g., <2% BLEU/MT/embedding drift threshold or model-specific metric).
Carlos: For batching/caching we need to list infra dependencies: async batching runtime changes, per-tenant batching config, key-value cache with eviction, metrics pipeline updates. Effort 2-6 depending on scope.
Lee: Customer-facing launch criteria idea:
- Quant: <3% regression on core prompts, >1.7x throughput improvement for target models, integration doc + SDK example
- Batching: tail p99 latency at target throughput within SLA bounds, clear per-route config
- Caching: cost reduction on prefix-heavy flows >20%, transparent invalidation and privacy docs
Maya: Sequencing proposal: 1) Quant spike + eval (2w) -> 2) Batching MVP (4w) parallel perf infra items -> 3) Caching pilot (3w) with rollout to Dedicated customers first. That keeps quick wins while we validate quality.
Jordan: I'm worried about simultaneous kernel and batching work interfering. Can we parallelize: quant spike on a forked kernel branch + batching as ops-layer changes? Should be doable if we isolate infra changes.
Priya: We'll need a labeling set for quality checks. I'll own creating the eval suite and thresholds.
Carlos: I'll map infra tasks and create a rough Gantt. Also recommend a canary plan: start with internal traffic, then one small customer, then gradual ramp. deploy-bot will handle staged rollouts.
deploy-bot: scheduled: canary-window 48h, auto-rollback on error-rate >1%.
Maya: OK action items:
- Priya: produce eval harness + baseline metrics by EOW (owner)
- Jordan: quant spike plan + perf checklist (2w)
- Carlos: infra dependency list + canary playbook (3d)
- Lee: Customer comms template + ask list for pilot customers
Maya: we'll reconvene after spike results to finalize RICE numbers and lock sprint slice. Any objections?
Jordan: no objections, +1 to spike-first.
Priya: +1, will start compiling benchmarks.
Carlos: +1, will share infra JIRA epic.
Lee: +1, will ping pilot customers.
Maya: thanks all — I'll publish this thread to the product folder and add the tentative schedule to the roadmap doc. :white_check_mark:
